task.title: Add automation-readiness runtime predicate
task.summary: Implement graph/runtime automation-readiness status so agents and daemon flows know when work is runnable, blocked, retryable, or promotable without inferring from chat.

goal.outcome: Automation can select or reject work from a deterministic readiness predicate instead of chat inference or roadmap status alone.
acceptance: Generated state exposes automation-readiness for tasks and sprints with states such as runnable, blocked, waiting, retryable, and promotable or equivalent source-backed categories.

Readiness evaluation considers executable task boundary, accepted decision/planning refs or approved exemption, gate policy, risk/approval state, scoped leases/worktree strategy, candidate files, model policy, blocker status, context-boundary plan, and deterministic next action.
The automation-readiness state is available to the focused state lens without requiring full graph output.
Agency planning and runtime runner refuse to schedule work whose readiness contract is missing, stale, blocked, ambiguous, or conflicts with active leases.
Wait/wake output names exact blockers and next safe actions using lease ids, branch refs, validation refs, publisher refs, or rebase requirements.
Tests cover runnable, blocked, waiting-on-lease, retryable-after-failure, and promotable-after-validation scenarios.
non_goals: Do not implement unbounded autonomous editing.
Do not bypass decision, planning, implementation, validation, task-close, ship-ready, publication, destructive, or approval gates.
Do not create a second competing runtime graph store.
Do not infer requirements from chat history when source refs are missing.
verification: wiki_gate/task-close linters for alignment, changed, generated-parity, and source-contract
